title: ST_Geometries
description: Returns the direct members of a geometry as a list, without recursing into nested collections.
kernels:
  - returns: list<geometry>
    args: [geometry]
  - returns: list<geography>
    args: [geography]
---

## Description

Returns the parts of a multi-geometry or the members of a geometry collection,
one level deep: a collection nested inside a collection is returned whole. A
geometry that is not a collection returns itself as the only member, even when
it is empty, while an empty multi-geometry or collection returns an empty list.
The members keep the input's spatial type and CRS, and NULL returns NULL.

Unlike `ST_Dump`, which recurses into nested collections down to their atomic
parts and records each part's position in a `path`, `ST_Geometries` returns
only the members themselves, matching Shapely's `get_parts()`. Combined with
`UNNEST`, it turns each member into its own row.

`UNNEST` currently returns the members as WKB rather than geometry, because it
drops the list's item type (apache/datafusion#26331); wrap it in
`ST_GeomFromWKB` (and `ST_SetSRID`, to keep a CRS) until that is fixed.

## Examples

```sql
SELECT ST_Geometries(ST_GeomFromText('MULTIPOINT ((10 40), (40 30), (20 20))'));
```

```sql
SELECT ST_Geometries(ST_GeomFromText('GEOMETRYCOLLECTION (POINT (1 2), GEOMETRYCOLLECTION (POINT (3 4), LINESTRING (0 0, 1 1)))'));
```

```sql
SELECT ST_GeomFromWKB(UNNEST(ST_Geometries(ST_GeomFromText('MULTIPOLYGON (((0 0, 1 0, 1 1, 0 0)), ((2 2, 3 2, 3 3, 2 2)))')))) AS part;
```
